sites.label: A
sites.name_ja: Almaty regional HQ (Esentai Tower, Al-Farabi Avenue)
sites.coord_note_ja: Nominatim way 1458250144 'Esentai Tower Business Center, 77/7 Al-Farabi Avenue' (43.2193,76.9293); Wikipedia 43.21905,76.92937
sites.building_ja: Esentai Tower, Al-Farabi Avenue 77/7: 36-storey, 162 m reinforced-concrete office/hotel tower completed 2008 (offices on floors 1-14, Ritz-Carlton above, LEED Silver 2016; Wikipedia). Office assumed on the 12th floor; standby generator serves common areas only (assumption)
sites.desc_ja: On Al-Farabi Avenue at the southern, upslope edge of the city center (Bostandyk district, about 870 m), next to the channelized Esentai river and 1.5 km west of the Kishi Almaty mudflow corridor. Almaty was destroyed by earthquakes in 1887 and 1911 (M8.0 Kemin, 37 km away) and lost about 500 people to the 1921 Kishi Almaty mudflow; the Medeu dam stopped the 1973 flow, and on 23 July 2015 a glacial-lake outburst mudflow hit the western outskirts (900 evacuated). The M7.0 Wushi earthquake of 22 January 2024 (270 km away) was felt in the city's high-rises with USGS community intensity 4.6 from 235 Almaty reports (USGS us7000lsze).
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard: earthquake High, landslide Medium, extreme heat Medium, wildfire High, river/urban flood Very low. For this tower the governing risks are strong shaking (design intensity MSK-64 9) with long elevator outages and facade/glass damage, winter smog and heavy snow, and mudflow risk confined to the river corridors east and west of the site rather than the building itself.

sites.name_ja: Atyrau branch office and logistics base (Bayterek Plaza, west bank)
sites.type_ja: Oil & gas services branch office and logistics base
sites.building_ja: Bayterek Plaza business centre, 25 Student (Studenchesky) Ave, west bank, about 450 m from the Zhaiyk embankment and 500 m south-west of the Central Bridge (OSM office building, Nominatim page_read). Floors, structure and year not verified - assumed 6-storey reinforced-concrete frame, 2010s; office on the 4th floor, yard and warehouse assumed in the Nursaya-3 industrial strip on the airport road.
sites.desc_ja: West-bank business district between Satpayev Street and the river, 450 m south of Tengizchevroil's head office (3 Satpayev St), 500 m from the regional akimat (seat of the regional flood operations staff) and 200 m from the Marriott Executive Apartments. In the record spring flood of 2024 the Atyrau gauge exceeded its critical level (553 cm vs 550 cm, mid-May) but the embankments held and the centre stayed dry; the site's exposure was indirect - staff whose families lived in flooded Kulsary (33,641 evacuated, April 2024), floodplain dacha evacuations, bridge and road restrictions and the use of the Tengiz rotation camps for evacuees.
sites.risk_note_ja: River flood High (ThinkHazard) but with weeks of lead time from the upstream gauges (Uralsk critical 850 cm, Atyrau 550 cm); urban ponding during the spring thaw; earthquake Very low. Extreme heat Medium (record 44.6 C) and severe winter cold (record -37.9 C) make power and heating continuity critical; hydrogen-sulfide air-pollution episodes; dependence on two road bridges, one airport (GUW) and the Atyrau-Kulsary-Tengiz road for the logistics chain.

sites.flood_trigger_ja: Zhaiyk floods are forecast weeks ahead. Triggers: Kazhydromet forecast of the Atyrau gauge approaching its 550 cm critical level (2024 peak 553 cm) or the Uralsk gauge passing 850 cm; MES/akimat evacuation orders for floodplain dachas, Balykshi or Zhumysker; a dike-breach report (as at Sokolok on 24 May 2024); or closure of the Central or Sultan Beibarys bridge. sites.building_ja: Nest One, 1A/1 Yangi Toshkent Street, Tashkent City International Business Center: 51-storey, 266.5 m mixed-use tower (offices, apartments, hotel, retail; 34 elevators), completed 2022 and opened 2023, the tallest building in Uzbekistan (Wikipedia). Office assumed on the 15th floor; standby generator serves common areas only (assumption) Alternative verified business-centre address for a smaller sales team: the Poytaxt business/trade centre, 9 Bukhara Street at Amir Temur Square (Nominatim node 4218887189, 41.3114,69.2750; not used in the demo).
sites.desc_ja: In the Tashkent City business district on the former Olmazor mahalla site, 600 m north of the Anhor canal and 2 km south-west of the Monument of Courage that marks the epicentre of the 26 April 1966 earthquake, which destroyed the adobe old city just north of here and left 200,000-300,000 people homeless. The district was built 2018-2023 to current seismic codes; recent stresses were the January 2023 cold wave with gas and power shortages, the record-level heat of July 2026 (44.3 C) and the November 2021 dust storm.
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard (Tashkent city): earthquake High, wildfire High, extreme heat Medium, water scarcity Medium, river/urban flood Low, landslide Low. For this tower the governing risks are strong shaking in seismic zone 8-9 with elevator entrapment and facade damage, summer heat with grid failures and winter gas/power shortages; flood exposure is limited to canal corridors and underpasses away from the site.

sites.label: D
sites.name_ja: Bishkek country office (Avangard Business Centre, Toktogul Street 125/1)
sites.coord_note_ja: Nominatim way 1186153469 (building=office 'Avangard - Business Centre', 125/1 Toktogul Street, Pervomaysky district, 720040) at 42.87274,74.59739; Tower B hosts PwC Kyrgyzstan on the 4th floor (PwC contact page, search_snippet)
sites.building_ja: Avangard Business Centre, Toktogul Street 125/1 (Towers A and B), a post-2010 reinforced-concrete office complex in the Golden Square between Chyngyz Aytmatov (Manas) Avenue and Togolok Moldo Street, next to the National Hospital. Storey count not verified (assumed about 9); office assumed on the 5th floor of Tower B; backup generator assumed to serve common areas only; district heating from the Bishkek CHP (assumptions)
sites.desc_ja: In the flat city centre (about 780 m), 1 km east of the channelized Ala-Archa river and 2.5 km west of the Alamudun, on the alluvial plain north of the Issyk-Ata fault. Bishkek lies in the 9-point (MSK-64) seismic zone: the 1885 Belovodsk (IX-X), 1911 Kemin M8.0 and 1938 Kemin-Chu M7.0 earthquakes struck the Chuy valley, USGS lists 18 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950 (latest 12 Aug 2026) and a Mw 7.5 Issyk-Ata scenario is modelled at about 2,400 deaths (Amey and Elliott 2023). Water hazards are river-specific: the Ala-Archa flooded Akhunbaev and Maldybaev streets after an ice jam on 16 Dec 2023 and triggered a mudflow readiness regime in July 2024, while the Great Chuy Canal crosses the north of the frame. Winter brings -30 C cold spells (state of emergency Dec 2012), CHP heating failures (Jan 2018, 2 Feb 2024) and some of the world's worst daily smog.
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard (Chuy Region; the Bishkek division has no data): earthquake High, landslide High, wildfire High, extreme heat Medium, river and urban flood Low, water scarcity Very low. For this mid-rise office the governing risks are strong shaking (design intensity 9) with stairway evacuation and elevator outage, winter heating/power failures and smog (coal season, CHP breakdowns), and heat above 35 C in July-August; mudflow and ice-jam risk is confined to the Ala-Archa and Alamudun corridors and the BChK strip, not the building itself.

sites.building_ja: Dushanbe Plaza, Rudaki Avenue: 20-storey, 92 m office/hotel tower opened September 2011 (about 40,000 m2; offices on floors 7-15, hotel apartments on 17-20, 12 elevators, two basement parking levels - Asia-Plus, search_snippet). Office assumed on the 9th floor; building generator assumed to serve common areas only (assumption)
sites.desc_ja: On Rudaki Avenue in the heart of the capital (Ismoili Somoni district, about 820 m), 600 m east of the Varzob (Dushanbinka) river, 500 m south of Rudaki Park and the Palace of Nations and 1 km from the CoES headquarters. Dushanbe sits in the 9-point seismic zone: the 1907 Qaratog M7.4 earthquake struck 99 km west (12,000-15,000 dead), the 1989 Gissar mb5.3 earthquake 14 km west killed 274 in loess flowslides, and the M5.2 Vahdat earthquake of 2013 shook the city (USGS, Wikipedia). Mudflows in the Varzob gorge cut the city's water supply in July 2004 (400,000 without clean water) and May 2016, and August 2023 rains killed 21 in the commuter districts.
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard (DRS division incl. Dushanbe): earthquake High, landslide High, urban flood High, wildfire High, extreme heat Medium, water scarcity Medium, river flood Low. For this tower the governing risks are strong shaking (MSK-64 9 design zone) with elevator outage and facade damage, loss of city water after Varzob mudflows, summer heat with power cuts, and winter heating/electricity failure; the building itself stands 600 m from the river corridor.

sites.name_ja: Ashgabat representative office (Olympic Business Center, 10 yyl Abadancylyk Avenue, Berzengi)
sites.coord_note_ja: Nominatim way 387583371 'Olympic Business Center, 10 yyl Abadancylyk (1945) sayoly, Kopetdag etraby, 744028' (building=commercial, building:levels 16). Alternatives verified in the same data: Paytagt Business Center (way 355588118, 37.8940,58.3902, hosts the Embassy of Japan), Berkarar Business Center (Ataturk St 82), Yyldyz Hotel business centre (37.9294,58.3332)
sites.building_ja: Olympic Business Center, 10 yyl Abadancylyk Avenue (1945 street), Berzengi: 16-storey white-marble-clad reinforced-concrete office building of the 2010s next to the Olympic complex (OSM building:levels 16; year and structure are assumptions - no building page found). Office assumed on the 11th floor with a 2-hour UPS; building generator serves lifts and lobby only (assumption)
sites.desc_ja: On 10 yyl Abadancylyk Avenue in Berzengi, the post-2000 government and diplomatic district on the upper (southern) piedmont of Ashgabat at about 270 m, 1.5 km west of the Embassy of Japan (Paytagt centre, same avenue) and 1 km south of the Olympic complex. Ashgabat lies in the MSK-64 intensity 9 zone and was destroyed by the Ms 7.3 earthquake of 6 October 1948 (epicentre 14 km north; 10,000-110,000 dead). Seasonal Kopet Dag mudflows are intercepted by the 2022 diversion canals 2-3 km to the south, while the flat central districts flooded after three days of rain on 15-17 May 2024. Summers reach 45-47 C (record 47.2 C, 30 June 2015) and dust storms arrive with spring cyclones.
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard (Ahal): earthquake High, river flood High, water scarcity High, wildfire High, extreme heat Medium, urban flood Low, landslide Low, cyclone Very low. For this 16-storey tower the governing risks are strong shaking (MSK-64 9 design zone; 1948 precedent), extreme heat with power-demand outages, and dust storms; mudflow and pluvial flood risk is confined to the canal belt south of Archabil and the Parahat lowlands rather than the building itself.

sites.districts_note_ja: Populations are the 17 December 2022 census counts shown on the English Wikipedia district pages (third_party; the four districts sum to 1,030,063, the city total on the Ashgabat page and in OSM). stat.gov.tm and citypopulation.de are blocked for fetching in this session; the WebSearch summary of stat.gov.tm gives the same four figures (search_snippet). Natural Earth has no separate Ashgabat city unit, so adm1 = TKM-352 Ahal.
sites.flood_trigger_ja: Flash flood / mudflow is a forecast-led hazard here: when Turkmenhydromet forecasts heavy rain (more than about 20 mm/day, typically March-May) or the Ministry of Defence civil-defence directorate issues a mudflow warning for the Kopet Dag foothills, staff living in Parahat 1-4 and along Ankara Street move cars out of underpasses and basements, avoid the Ashgabat Canal and the southern diversion-canal belt, and the office switches to remote work for the day; after the May 2024 flooding, roads in the centre were impassable for a day. Procedure and thresholds are assumptions for the demo.
